title: Dimension lower bound for a polynomial quotient over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $m\ge t\ge0$ integers, and $f_1,\dots,f_t\in k[x_1,\dots,x_m]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring]. If $T=k[x_1,\dots,x_m]/(f_1,\dots,f_t)$ is nonzero, then the Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] of $\operatorname{Spec}T$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is at least $m-t$.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), applying Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation) at a maximal ideal containing the equations; same lower bound implicit in Tag 00ST

proof.text: Put P = k[x_1,...,x_m], J = span(range f), and T = P/J. Choose a maximal ideal n of the nonzero quotient with Ideal.exists_maximal (the zero-ideal case of lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal). Its comap M along the surjective quotient map is maximal by Ideal.comap_isMaximal_of_surjective. Each generator maps to zero, hence belongs to M; Ideal.map_comap_of_surjective identifies M/J with n.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35834-35849: choose a maximal ideal containing the equations; existence also follows from Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), item (2)

proof.text: Apply MvPolynomial.ringKrullDim_localizationAtMaximal to M and IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height to get height(M) = m. The polynomial ring and its quotient are Noetherian by the canonical Mathlib instances, specializing lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian. Ideal.height_le_height_add_encard_of_subset applied to range f gives m <= height(n) + encard(range f). Set.encard_image_le bounds that cardinality by t, even if equations repeat. The maximal ideal n has finite height by Noetherianity; write height(n) = d, convert to natural numbers, and deduce m - t <= d.

source.place: Algebra, paragraph following Definition Tag 00S9 (definition-lci-field), lines 35834-35849, using Tag 00OP (lemma-dim-affine-space) and Tag 00KW (lemma-one-equation) t times

proof.text: The surjective k-algebra map Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ gives the finite polynomial presentation of T. Apply topologicalKrullDimAt_eq_ringKrullDim_localizationAtMaximal at n and IsLocalization.AtPrime.ringKrullDim_eq_height to identify its local topological dimension with height(n) = d. Finally topologicalKrullDim_eq_iSup_topologicalKrullDimAt and le_iSup give the desired global bound.
